I'm completing a take-home assignment for a Program Delivery Manager position at KnowledgeCity. The full brief is pasted below. Please read it carefully. Do NOT write any code or files yet.

My product decision: I'm building a Tip and Bill Splitter web app.

Who it's for and why: groups of friends, family or colleagues eating out together. When the bill arrives, three things go wrong: people aren't sure what tip is fair, splitting evenly leaves awkwardleftover cents that make the shares not add up, and when one person pays for everyone, working out who owes what based on what each person ordered (plus a fair share of tax and tip) is slow and error-prone on a phone calculator. I chose this because the maths is simple but the edge cases (rounding, tiny/huge amounts, invalid input) are exactly where real calculators get things wrong, which lets me show careful requirements and testing in a small app.

I see two user types:
- Diner: one person at the table who wants to settle on a fair tip and split evenly.
- Bill Organiser: the person who paid for the whole group and needs to collect a different amount from each person based on what they ordered.

Before we start:
1. Summarise the deliverables and grading criteria back to me in your own words so I can check you've understood them.
2. Ask me up to 5 clarifying questions where a wrong assumption would be expensive later (scope, rounding, limits, users).

--- BRIEF ---

Take-Home Assignment: Build a Calculator Web App with an AI Coding Tool
KnowledgeCity, Technology Division
About this assignment
Thank you for your interest in joining KnowledgeCity. Our product software is built with AI coding tools, and the people in product and delivery roles direct that work: they decide who a product is for, define what it must do, and check that what the AI builds is correct. This assignment asks you to do the same on a small scale.
You will build a calculator web application with an AI coding tool and send us three things: the working source code, the transcript of your session with the AI tool, and a short set of product documents. The code shows us the result, the transcript shows us how you got there, and the documents show us how you think about users and requirements.
Plan for about 2 to 4 hours. A small app that works and is well specified is worth more to us than a large one that does not.
The task
Build a calculator that runs in a web browser, using an AI coding tool to write the code.
The kind of calculator is your choice: a basic arithmetic calculator, a scientific calculator, a loan or mortgage calculator, a tip and bill splitter, or anything else that calculates. Deciding who it is for and what problem it solves is part of the assignment, so state your choice and your reasons in the README.
Requirements
It runs in a current version of Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari.
A reviewer can start it on their own computer by following your README, with no paid accounts, API keys or cloud services. A public URL where the app is already running is welcome in addition to this, not instead of it.
Any programming language, framework or library is fine.
Every user story you mark as Implemented works in the running app exactly as its acceptance criteria describe.
Invalid input and error cases, such as division by zero, produce a clear message, never a crash or a wrong result.
Using an AI coding tool
Use any AI coding tool: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, Gemini CLI or similar.
The AI tool writes the code. Your job is to direct it: explain the problem, give it the context it needs, review what it produces, test the result and correct it.
If you change any code by hand, list those changes in the README.
You may work across several sessions or several tools. Send the transcript of every session.
You may use AI to help write the product documents too. You are responsible for their content and should be ready to explain any part of them.
What to submit
Source code
The complete source code, without installed dependencies or build output (for example, leave out node_modules, virtual environments and dist folders).
A README file in the root folder that covers: what the app is and who it is for; the prerequisites (for example, Node.js 20); the exact commands to install and start the app; how to run the tests, if you wrote any; which AI tool and model you used; any code you changed by hand; and any assumptions you made.
Session transcript
The transcript is the full record of your conversation with the AI tool: your prompts exactly as you typed them and the tool's responses, from the first message to the last. It shows us how you work with AI, so it matters as much as the code.
Export it with the tool's own export feature. In Claude Code, the /export command saves the conversation to a file, and session logs are also kept under ~/.claude/projects/. The OpenAI Codex CLI keeps session logs under ~/.codex/sessions/. Other tools usually have an export or copy option on the chat.
Send the export as it is. A summary of the session, including one the AI tool writes for you at the end, does not count as the transcript.
Before you send it, remove any passwords, API keys or tokens, and change nothing else.
Product documents
Write three documents, in this order, because each one builds on the one before it.
Document
Answers
Format of each entry
App Roles
Who uses the app
"A [role] is [who this person is and their situation]. They can [what they see and do in the app]. They must never [what the app must prevent]", where the last part applies.
Jobs To Be Done
Why they use it
"When [situation], I want to [motivation], so I can [expected outcome]." Each job names the role it belongs to.
User Stories with Acceptance Criteria
How the app helps them get the job done
"As a [role], I want [capability], so that [benefit]." Each story names the job it serves and has acceptance criteria and a status.


App Roles. A calculator may have one role or several. Either is fine, as long as each role describes a real kind of person and explains how their needs differ from the other roles.
Jobs To Be Done. A job describes what the person needs to get done whether or not your app exists, so it does not mention your app or its features. If a job cannot be written without naming a button or a screen, it is a feature, not a job.
User Stories. Every story names the job it serves, and every job names the role it belongs to. A story that serves no job does not belong in the list.
Acceptance criteria. Write specific, testable statements of how the app behaves, preferably as "Given [starting state], when [action], then [observable result]". Cover the normal case and the cases where things go wrong: invalid input, boundary values, very large or very small numbers, and what happens when the user carries on after a result or an error.
Status. Mark each story Implemented or Not implemented, based on what the app does today. Stories you would build next are welcome, marked Not implemented.
Markdown, PDF, Word or Google Docs are all fine. Put the files in a docs folder, or link to them from the README.
Example of the format
This example uses a meeting room booking app, so it does not overlap with your calculator.
App Role. "An Office Employee is a staff member who books rooms for their own meetings. They can see which rooms are free and see their own bookings. They can create and cancel their own bookings. They must never cancel another person's booking."
Job J-1 (Office Employee). "When I need to meet colleagues in person, I want to secure a suitable space in advance, so I can hold the meeting without searching for a free room on the day."
User Story S-1 (serves J-1, Implemented). "As an Office Employee, I want to see which rooms are free at a time I choose, so that I can book one without checking each room."
Given rooms A and B are free from 10:00 to 11:00 and room C is booked, when I search for 10:00 to 11:00, then I see rooms A and B and I do not see room C.
Given I enter an end time earlier than the start time, when I search, then I see the message "End time must be after the start time" and no rooms are listed.
Packaging and sending
Organize the package like this (the layout of the source folder is up to you):
firstname-lastname-calculator/
  README.md
  src/
  docs/
    app-roles.md
    jobs-to-be-done.md
    user-stories.md
  transcripts/
    session-01.md
When you receive this assignment, reply to confirm and tell us when you expect to submit.
Email your submission to the HR contact who sent you this assignment, by the deadline in their email.
Share the package as a link: a Google Drive folder or a Git repository on GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket, open to anyone who has the link. Many email systems, Gmail included, block .zip attachments that contain code, so a link is more reliable than an attachment.
Use the subject line: Take-home assignment: [the role you applied for], [your full name].
In the email, include the link, the live URL if you deployed the app, the AI tools and models you used, and roughly how long you spent.
How we review your submission
It works. We follow your README on a clean computer and use the app the way one of your users would. Automated tests are welcome, and we still check the behavior by hand.
Product thinking. The roles describe real people with different needs, the jobs are free of solutions, every story traces to a job, and the acceptance criteria are testable and cover error and edge cases.
Working with AI. From the transcript: how you framed the problem, what context you gave the tool, how you checked its output, and which mistakes you caught and fixed.
Accuracy. The documents and the README describe what was actually built. A story honestly marked Not implemented counts for more than an overstated claim.
Delivery and communication. You told us when to expect your submission and delivered by then, and the package is clear and easy to review.
Be ready to walk us through your submission and explain your decisions in a follow-up conversation.
Questions
If anything in this assignment is unclear, ask your HR contact. You can also make a reasonable assumption and write it down in the README. How you handle open questions is part of what we look at.

input.content:
# App Roles

The app has two roles. The same person can be a Diner one evening and a Bill Organiser the next. What separates the roles is the situation at the table: whether the group shares the bill equally, or one person has paid and needs to be paid back for what each person ordered.

## Diner

A **Diner** is one person in a group eating out. The group has agreed to share the bill equally. When the bill arrives, the Diner usually has only a phone in hand. They want a quick answer on what tip is fair and what each person pays, and they want those shares to add up exactly to the bill so no one argues over leftover money.

They can:
- enter the amounts on the receipt: the subtotal, plus tax and service charges
- pick a tip percentage or type their own
- enter the number of people
- see the tip amount, the grand total, and what each person pays

They must never:
- be shown per-person shares that do not add up exactly to the grand total
- be shown a tip, total or share calculated from input the app has rejected

## Bill Organiser

A **Bill Organiser** is the person who paid the whole bill for the group, for example with one card. Each person ordered something different, so equal shares would be unfair. The Organiser needs to collect a different amount from each person: what that person ordered, plus a fair part of the tax, service charges and tip.

The Organiser's needs differ from the Diner's in three ways:
- they work person by person, not with one headcount
- fairness here means "in proportion to what you ordered", not "equal"
- they carry the financial risk: if the amounts they collect fall short of the receipt, they pay the difference themselves

They can:
- enter the receipt subtotal, tax and service charges, and tip
- list each person, with an optional name and the amount that person ordered
- add or remove people
- see what each person owes, broken down into their order and their share of tax, charges and tip
- see whether the amounts owed add up to the receipt total

They must never:
- be shown amounts owed whose sum differs from the receipt total without a visible warning that states the difference
- be shown a share of tax, charges and tip for any person that is not in proportion to what that person ordered, apart from the at most 1 cent needed to make the total add up exactly
- be shown amounts calculated from input the app has rejected

# Jobs To Be Done

Each job describes what the person needs to get done whether or not this app exists. No job mentions the app or its features.

## Diner

**J-1 (Diner)**
When the bill arrives at the end of a meal, I want to decide on a tip that is fair for the service, so I can leave a tip without overpaying or looking stingy.

**J-2 (Diner)**
When my group has agreed to share the bill equally, I want everyone's share worked out so that the shares add up exactly to the bill, so we can all pay and leave without arguing over leftover money.

## Bill Organiser

**J-3 (Bill Organiser)**
When I have paid for a group meal on my own, I want to know how much each person owes for what they had, including their fair part of the tax, charges and tip, so I can get my money back without anyone paying for someone else's food.

**J-4 (Bill Organiser)**
When I ask people to pay me back, I want to be sure the amounts I ask for cover the whole bill, so I am not left out of pocket.

**J-5 (Bill Organiser)**
When I have worked out what everyone owes, I want to tell each person their amount quickly, so I can collect the money the same day while everyone remembers the meal.

# User Stories with Acceptance Criteria

> **Status note.** This document was written before the app was built. Stories planned for the first version are marked **Not implemented (planned for v1)**. Each one changes to **Implemented** only after every one of its acceptance criteria has been checked by hand in the running app. Stories marked **Not implemented (backlog)** are possible next steps.

## Shared definitions

These rules apply to every story. The acceptance criteria refer to them.

**Money inputs** cover the subtotal, the tax and service charges, and each person's ordered amount.
- Leading and trailing spaces are ignored.
- A valid amount is digits with an optional single decimal point and at most 2 decimal places. Examples: `1250`, `1250.5`, `1250.50`, `.5`, `12.`
- Commas, letters, currency symbols, `+`, `e` notation and more than one decimal point are rejected.

**Tip percentage**
- A preset (0%, 10%, 15%, 20%) or a custom value from 0 to 100, with at most 2 decimal places.
- The tip is calculated on the subtotal before tax and service charges.
- 10% is selected when the page opens.

**Tax and service charges** is one optional amount field. Leaving it empty means 0. It covers GST, sales tax and any service charge printed on the receipt.

**Arithmetic**
- All calculations use whole cents, so there are no floating-point errors.
- The tip is rounded to the nearest cent, with exact halves rounded up. For example, 1.5 cents becomes 2 cents.

**Display**
- All results are shown with 2 decimal places and comma thousands separators, for example `1,260.00`.
- No currency symbol is shown.

**Live results**
- Results update as soon as every input is valid.
- While any input is invalid or missing, no results are shown. The results area shows "Fix the highlighted fields to see the split."
- A field's error message appears when the user leaves that field.

**Limits**

| Input | Allowed range |
|---|---|
| Subtotal | 0.01 to 1,000,000.00 |
| Tax and service charges | 0 to 1,000,000.00 |
| Ordered amount per person | 0.01 to 1,000,000.00 |
| Number of people (even split) | Whole number from 1 to 50 |
| People listed (split by order) | 1 to 50 |

**Error messages**

| Case | Message |
|---|---|
| Subtotal empty | "Enter the bill subtotal." |
| Not a valid number | "Enter an amount using digits and an optional decimal point, e.g. 1250.50." |
| Negative amount | "Amount can't be negative." |
| More than 2 decimal places | "Use at most 2 decimal places." |
| Subtotal below 0.01 | "Subtotal must be at least 0.01." |
| Subtotal, tax or ordered amount above 1,000,000.00 | "Amount can't be more than 1,000,000.00." |
| Custom tip empty | "Enter a tip percentage." |
| Custom tip out of range or not a number | "Tip must be a number from 0 to 100." |
| Number of people invalid | "Number of people must be a whole number from 1 to 50." |
| Ordered amount empty or below 0.01 | "Enter what this person ordered (at least 0.01)." |

---

## Diner stories

### S-1: Enter the receipt amounts
**Serves:** J-1 · **Role:** Diner · **Status:** Not implemented (planned for v1)

As a Diner, I want to enter the amounts printed on the receipt and be told straight away if something is wrong, so that the tip and split are based on the real bill.

- Given the page has just opened, when I look at the inputs, then the subtotal is empty, tax and service charges is empty, 10% tip is selected, and the number of people is 2.
- Given I enter subtotal `1000` and leave tax empty, when the results appear, then tax and service charges is treated as 0.00.
- Given I enter subtotal ` 1000.50 ` with spaces around it, when I leave the field, then it is accepted as 1,000.50.
- Given I enter subtotal `.5`, when the results appear, then the subtotal is used as 0.50.
- Given I enter subtotal `abc`, `1,000`, `1e3` or `10.0.5`, when I leave the field, then I see "Enter an amount using digits and an optional decimal point, e.g. 1250.50." and no results are shown.
- Given I enter subtotal `-20`, when I leave the field, then I see "Amount can't be negative." and no results are shown.
- Given I enter subtotal `10.555`, when I leave the field, then I see "Use at most 2 decimal places." and no results are shown.
- Given I enter subtotal `0` or `0.00`, when I leave the field, then I see "Subtotal must be at least 0.01." and no results are shown.
- Given I enter subtotal `1000000.01`, when I leave the field, then I see "Amount can't be more than 1,000,000.00." and no results are shown.
- Given I enter subtotal `1000000.00`, when the results appear, then the subtotal is accepted.
- Given I clear the subtotal after entering it, when I leave the field, then I see "Enter the bill subtotal." and no results are shown.
- Given the subtotal shows an error, when I correct it to `1000`, then the error message disappears and results appear.

### S-2: Choose a tip and see its amount
**Serves:** J-1 · **Role:** Diner · **Status:** Not implemented (planned for v1)

As a Diner, I want to choose a common tip percentage or type my own and see the tip amount and grand total, so that I can settle on a fair tip quickly.

- Given subtotal `1000` and tax `160`, when 10% is selected, then I see tip 100.00 and total 1,260.00. The tip is calculated on the subtotal, not on subtotal plus tax.
- Given subtotal `1000` and tax `160`, when I change the tip from 10% to 20%, then the results update immediately to tip 200.00 and total 1,360.00.
- Given subtotal `10.05` and tax empty, when 15% is selected, then I see tip 1.51 (1.5075 rounded) and total 11.56.
- Given subtotal `0.10` and tax empty, when 15% is selected, then I see tip 0.02 (1.5 cents rounded up) and total 0.12.
- Given subtotal `1000`, when 0% is selected, then I see tip 0.00 and total equal to subtotal plus tax.
- Given subtotal `200`, when I enter custom tip `12.5`, then I see tip 25.00.
- Given subtotal `1000`, when I enter custom tip `100`, then I see tip 1,000.00.
- Given I enter custom tip `100.01`, `-5` or `ten`, when I leave the field, then I see "Tip must be a number from 0 to 100." and no results are shown.
- Given I choose custom tip and leave it empty, when I leave the field, then I see "Enter a tip percentage." and no results are shown.
- Given subtotal `1000000`, tax `1000000` and custom tip `100`, when the results appear, then I see tip 1,000,000.00 and total 3,000,000.00 exactly.

### S-3: Split the total evenly so the shares add up exactly
**Serves:** J-2 · **Role:** Diner · **Status:** Not implemented (planned for v1)

As a Diner, I want the grand total split evenly between the number of people, with any leftover cents shown openly, so that the shares add up exactly to the bill.

- Given a total of 1,260.00, when I enter 4 people, then I see "Each person pays 315.00" and "4 shares add up to 1,260.00".
- Given a total of 100.00 (subtotal `100`, tax empty, tip 0%), when I enter 3 people, then I see "1 person pays 33.34" and "2 people pay 33.33" and "3 shares add up to 100.00".
- Given a total of 3,000,000.00, when I enter 7 people, then I see "6 people pay 428,571.43" and "1 person pays 428,571.42" and "7 shares add up to 3,000,000.00".
- Given a total of 0.02 (subtotal `0.02`, tip 0%), when I enter 3 people, then I see "2 people pay 0.01" and "1 person pays 0.00" and "3 shares add up to 0.02".
- Given any valid total, when I enter 1 person, then I see "Each person pays" followed by the full total.
- Given any valid total, when I enter 50 people, then the split is shown.
- Given I enter `0`, `51`, `2.5`, `-3`, `two`, or leave it empty, when I leave the people field, then I see "Number of people must be a whole number from 1 to 50." and no results are shown.
- Given results are shown for 3 people, when I change it to 4, then the results update immediately without pressing any button.
- Given results are shown, when I change any input to an invalid value, then the old results disappear, the field's error is shown, and "Fix the highlighted fields to see the split." appears. When I correct it, then results reappear for the new values.
- Given I have entered values, when I press "Reset", then all inputs return to their opening state as described in S-1, and no results or errors are shown.

### S-4: Round everyone's share up to a whole amount
**Serves:** J-2 · **Role:** Diner · **Status:** Not implemented (backlog)

As a Diner, I want the option for everyone to pay the same amount rounded up to a whole number, with the extra added to the tip, so that we can pay in notes or round transfers.

- Given a total of 100.00 and 3 people, when I turn on "Round up shares", then I see "Each person pays 34.00" and "Extra tip from rounding: 2.00".

# App Roles

The app has two roles. Their needs differ because a Diner's group shares the bill equally, so fairness means equal shares that add up exactly to the bill. A Bill Organiser has already paid the whole bill, so fairness means each person pays in proportion to what they ordered. Any shortfall comes out of the Organiser's own pocket.

## Diner

A Diner is one person in a group eating out who, when the bill arrives, wants to settle on a fair tip and work out an equal share for everyone, usually with only a phone in hand. They can enter the receipt subtotal and any tax and service charges, choose a preset or custom tip percentage, enter the number of people, and see the tip amount, the grand total and what each person pays. They must never be shown per-person shares that do not add up exactly to the grand total.

## Bill Organiser

A Bill Organiser is the person who paid the whole bill for a group in which everyone ordered different things, and who now needs to collect a different amount back from each person. They can enter the receipt subtotal, any tax and service charges and a tip percentage, list each person with an optional name and the amount they ordered, add or remove people, and see what each person owes as their order plus a share of tax, charges and tip, along with whether the amounts owed add up to the receipt total. They must never be shown amounts owed that add up to a different figure from the receipt total without a visible warning stating the difference, nor a share of tax, charges and tip for any person that is out of proportion to what they ordered, beyond the single cent needed to make the total add up exactly.

# User Stories with Acceptance Criteria

> **Status note.** This document was written before the app was built, so every story is **Not implemented**. A story changes to **Implemented** only after every one of its acceptance criteria has been checked by hand in the running app. "Planned for" shows whether a story is in scope for the first version (v1) or a possible next step (Backlog).

## Shared definitions

These rules apply to every story. The acceptance criteria refer to them.

### Money inputs

Money inputs cover the subtotal, the tax and service charges, each person's ordered amount, and a shared item's amount.

- Spaces before and after the value are ignored.
- A valid amount is digits with an optional single decimal point and at most 2 decimal places. Examples: `1250`, `1250.5`, `1250.50`, `.5`, `12.`, `007`.
- Commas and currency symbols or codes are rejected with their own message. This covers `$ € £ ₹ ₨`, and `Rs`, `Rs.` or `PKR` at the start or end.
- When an input breaks more than one rule, only the first matching message is shown, in this order:
  1. empty
  2. comma or currency symbol
  3. negative (starts with `-`)
  4. not a valid number (letters, `e` notation, `+`, more than one decimal point)
  5. more than 2 decimal places
  6. below the minimum
  7. above the maximum

### Tip percentage

- The tip is a preset (0%, 10%, 15%, 20%) or a custom value from 0 to 100 with at most 2 decimal places.
- A single trailing `%` is accepted and ignored. For example, `15%` means 15.
- 10% is selected when the page opens.
- The tip is calculated on the subtotal, before tax and service charges.

### Tax and service charges

This is one optional field. Leaving it empty means 0. It covers GST, sales tax and any service charge printed on the receipt.

### Arithmetic

- All calculations use whole cents.
- The tip is rounded to the nearest cent, with exact halves rounded up. For example, 1.5 cents becomes 2 cents.
- Results must be exact at every allowed limit. At the maximum values, some intermediate products in the Split by order calculation exceed 9,007,199,254,740,991 (the largest whole number JavaScript's normal numbers store exactly). The implementation must therefore use exact integer arithmetic, for example BigInt. S-6 contains a test case for this.

### Display

- Results show 2 decimal places and comma thousands separators, for example `1,260.00`.
- No currency symbol is shown.

### Live results

- Results update as soon as every input is valid. There is no Calculate button.
- A field's error message appears under that field when the user leaves it.
- While any field shows an error, no results are shown, and the results area says "Fix the highlighted fields to see the split."
- While a required field is still empty and no field shows an error, the results area says "Fill in the fields above to see the split."

### Limits

| Input | Allowed |
|---|---|
| Subtotal | 0.01 to 1,000,000.00 |
| Tax and service charges | 0 to 1,000,000.00 (empty = 0) |
| Ordered amount per person | 0.01 to 1,000,000.00 |
| Custom tip | 0 to 100, at most 2 decimal places |
| Number of people (Split evenly) | Whole number from 1 to 50 |
| People listed (Split by order) | 1 to 50 rows |
| Person's name | Optional, up to 30 characters |

### Error messages

| Case | Message |
|---|---|
| Subtotal empty | "Enter the bill subtotal." |
| Comma or currency symbol in any money input | "Remove commas and currency symbols, e.g. 1250.50." |
| Negative money input | "Amount can't be negative." |
| Money input is not a valid number | "Enter an amount using digits and an optional decimal point, e.g. 1250.50." |
| More than 2 decimal places (money input or custom tip) | "Use at most 2 decimal places." |
| Subtotal below 0.01 | "Subtotal must be at least 0.01." |
| Any money input above 1,000,000.00 | "Amount can't be more than 1,000,000.00." |
| Custom tip empty | "Enter a tip percentage." |
| Custom tip not a number, negative, or above 100 | "Tip must be a number from 0 to 100." |
| Number of people invalid | "Number of people must be a whole number from 1 to 50." |
| Ordered amount empty or below 0.01 | "Enter what this person ordered (at least 0.01)." |

### S-6: See what each person owes, with tax and tip shared in proportion
**Serves:** J-3 · **Role:** Bill Organiser · **Status:** Not implemented · **Planned for:** v1

As a Bill Organiser, I want to see what each person owes, made up of their order plus a share of tax, charges and tip in proportion to their order, so that nobody pays for someone else's food.

How shares are worked out:
- Each person's share of tax and tip is their ordered amount divided by the total of all ordered amounts, multiplied by tax plus tip.
- Each share is rounded down to the cent.
- Leftover cents go one at a time to the people with the largest remainders. Ties go to the person higher in the list.

The results show one row per person with three columns, "Ordered", "Share of tax and tip" and "Owes", followed by a total row.

**Normal case**
- Given subtotal `100`, tax `16` and tip 10%, and Ali ordered `60` and Sara ordered `40`, when results appear, then:
  - Ali: Ordered 60.00, Share 15.60, Owes 75.60
  - Sara: Ordered 40.00, Share 10.40, Owes 50.40
  - the total row shows 126.00 and "Matches the receipt total."
- Given subtotal `30`, tax `1` and tip 0%, and three people each ordered `10`, when results appear, then Person 1 owes 10.34, Person 2 owes 10.33 and Person 3 owes 10.33. The total is 31.00 and the tie goes to the person higher in the list.

**Invalid input**
- Given every row is valid, when I change the subtotal to `abc`, then no amounts owed are shown and the results area says "Fix the highlighted fields to see the split."
- Given every other input is valid, when I paste `Rs 60` as Ali's amount, then I see "Remove commas and currency symbols, e.g. 1250.50." on Ali's row and no amounts owed are shown.

**Boundary values**
- Given subtotal `100`, tax empty and tip 0%, and Ali ordered `60` and Sara ordered `40`, when results appear, then Ali owes 60.00 and Sara owes 40.00, with each share 0.00.
- Given one person whose ordered amount equals subtotal `100`, with tax `16` and tip 10%, when results appear, then they owe 126.00.
- Given subtotal `100`, tax empty and tip 15%, and Person 1 ordered `0.01` and Person 2 ordered `99.99`, when results appear, then:
  - Person 1 owes 0.01 (share 0.00)
  - Person 2 owes 114.99 (share 15.00)
  - the total is 115.00, and the leftover cent goes to the person with the larger remainder
- Given subtotal `0.50`, tax `0.01` and tip 0%, and 50 people each ordered `0.01`, when results appear, then Person 1 owes 0.02, Persons 2 to 50 each owe 0.01, and the total is 0.51.

**Very large and very small numbers**
- Given subtotal `1000000`, tax `1000000` and tip 100%, and Person 1 ordered `999999.99` and Person 2 ordered `0.01`, when results appear, then:
  - Person 1: Share 1,999,999.98, Owes 2,999,999.97
  - Person 2: Share 0.02, Owes 0.03
  - the total is 3,000,000.00 and "Matches the receipt total." is shown

  This case fails if the implementation does not use exact integer arithmetic.
- Given subtotal `0.03`, tax `0.01` and tip 0%, and three people each ordered `0.01`, when results appear, then Person 1 owes 0.02, Person 2 owes 0.01 and Person 3 owes 0.01, and the total is 0.04.

**Carrying on after a result or an error**
- Given results are shown, when I change Ali's amount from `60` to `50`, then every row and the total update immediately.
- Given results are shown for 3 people, when I remove one, then the shares are recalculated for the remaining 2.
- Given results are shown, when any input becomes invalid, then all amounts owed disappear. When it is fixed, then they reappear for the current values.

content.text:
1	# App Roles
2	
3	The app has two roles. Their needs differ because a Diner's group shares the bill equally, so fairness means equal shares that add up exactly to the bill. A Bill Organiser has already paid the whole bill, so fairness means each person pays in proportion to what they ordered. Any shortfall comes out of the Organiser's own pocket.
4	
5	## Diner
6	
7	A Diner is one person in a group eating out who, when the bill arrives, wants to settle on a fair tip and work out an equal share for everyone, usually with only a phone in hand. They can enter the receipt subtotal and any tax and service charges, choose a preset or custom tip percentage, enter the number of people, and see the tip amount, the grand total and what each person pays. They must never be shown per-person shares that do not add up exactly to the grand total.
8	
9	## Bill Organiser
10	
11	A Bill Organiser is the person who paid the whole bill for a group in which everyone ordered different things, and who now needs to collect a different amount back from each person. They can enter the receipt subtotal, any tax and service charges and a tip percentage, list each person with an optional name and the amount they ordered, add or remove people, and see what each person owes as their order plus a share of tax, charges and tip, along with whether the amounts owed add up to the receipt total. They must never be shown amounts owed that add up to a different figure from the receipt total without a visible warning stating the difference, nor a share of tax, charges and tip for any person that is out of proportion to what they ordered, beyond the single cent needed to make the total add up exactly.
12

1	# User Stories with Acceptance Criteria
2	
3	> **Status note.** This document was written before the app was built, so every story is **Not implemented**. A story changes to **Implemented** only after every one of its acceptance criteria has been checked by hand in the running app. "Planned for" shows whether a story is in scope for the first version (v1) or a possible next step (Backlog).
4	
5	## Shared definitions

# User Stories with Acceptance Criteria

> **Status note.** This document was written before the app was built, so every story is **Not implemented**. A story changes to **Implemented** only after every one of its acceptance criteria has been checked by hand in the running app. "Planned for" shows whether a story is in scope for the first version (v1) or a possible next step (Backlog).

## Traceability

| Story | Serves | Role | Planned for |
|---|---|---|---|
| S-1 Enter the receipt amounts | J-1 | Diner | v1 |
| S-2 Choose a tip and see its amount | J-1 | Diner | v1 |
| S-3 Split the total evenly | J-2 | Diner | v1 |
| S-4 Round everyone's share up | J-2 | Diner | Backlog |
| S-10 Enter the receipt amounts when splitting by order | J-3 | Bill Organiser | v1 |
| S-5 List each person and what they ordered | J-3 | Bill Organiser | v1 |
| S-6 See what each person owes | J-3 | Bill Organiser | v1 |
| S-7 Be warned when the amounts don't cover the bill | J-4 | Bill Organiser | v1 |
| S-8 Split a shared item | J-3 | Bill Organiser | Backlog |
| S-9 Copy a summary of who owes what | J-5 | Bill Organiser | Backlog |

J-5 is served only by a backlog story, so the first version does not help with it.

## Shared definitions

These rules apply to every story. The acceptance criteria refer to them.

### Layout and controls

- **Mode.** Two options at the top of the page: "Split evenly" and "Split by order". "Split evenly" is selected when the page opens.
- **Receipt fields.** These are shared by both modes:
  - "Subtotal"
  - "Tax and service charges"
  - the tip options, a row of five choices: "0%", "10%", "15%", "20%" and "Custom"
- **Custom tip.** Choosing "Custom" shows a text field labelled "Custom tip (%)". It is empty the first time it is shown, and it keeps what was typed if the user picks a preset and then picks "Custom" again.
- **Split evenly** has one field, "Number of people".
- **Split by order** has a list of rows. Each row has a "Name" field, an "Ordered" amount field and a "Remove" control. Below the list is an "Add person" control.
- **Reset** is a control at the bottom of the page.

### Results area

**Split evenly.** These lines appear in this order:
1. "Subtotal" and the amount
2. "Tax and service charges" and the amount
3. "Tip (P%)" and the amount, where P is the percentage as chosen or typed (for example "Tip (12.5%)")
4. "Total" and the amount
5. the share lines, described in S-3

**Split by order:**
1. The same four receipt lines.
2. A table with one row per person and three columns: "Ordered", "Share of tax and tip" and "Owes".
3. A total row showing the sum of "Owes", with the receipt check message from S-7.

The receipt check message is either "Matches the receipt total." or a message stating the difference.

### Validation timing

- On every keystroke, every input is checked and the results are recalculated.
- An input that holds an invalid value is outlined in red straight away, and the results disappear straight away. A result is never shown for values that are no longer on screen.
- The error message text under a field appears when the user leaves that field. Once it is showing, it updates or disappears on every keystroke.
- A required field that is empty and has never been left is not an error yet. Once the user leaves it empty, it shows its error.
- The results area message:
  - while any input is invalid: "Fix the highlighted fields to see the split."
  - otherwise, while any required field is empty: "Fill in the fields above to see the split."
  - otherwise, the results

### Switching mode

- The receipt fields (subtotal, tax and service charges, and tip) are shared between the two modes. Switching keeps them.
- "Number of people" and the Split by order list are kept separately. Switching away from a mode and back restores what was in it.
- The first time "Split by order" is opened, it shows 2 empty unnamed rows, whatever the number of people in "Split evenly".

### Reset

Pressing "Reset" does the following, in both modes:
- clears the subtotal and tax and service charges
- selects 10% tip and empties the custom tip field
- sets the number of people to 2
- returns the Split by order list to 2 empty unnamed rows
- turns off any options
- removes all errors

The mode that is currently selected stays selected.

### Money inputs

Money inputs are the subtotal, the tax and service charges, each person's ordered amount, and a shared item's amount.

- Spaces before and after the value are ignored.
- A valid amount is digits with an optional single decimal point and at most 2 decimal places. Examples: `1250`, `1250.5`, `1250.50`, `.5`, `12.`, `007`.
- An input counts as containing a comma or currency symbol if:
  - it contains a comma or any of `$ € £ ₹ ₨` anywhere, or
  - it starts or ends with `Rs`, `Rs.` or `PKR`, in any letter case, with or without a space. Examples: `Rs 1250`, `rs1250`, `1250Rs`, `pkr 1250`.
- When an input breaks more than one rule, only the first matching message is shown, in this order:
  1. empty
  2. comma or currency symbol
  3. negative (starts with `-`)
  4. not a valid number (letters, `e` notation, `+`, more than one decimal point)
  5. more than 2 decimal places
  6. below the minimum
  7. above the maximum

### Custom tip

- Spaces before and after the value are ignored, and so is a single trailing `%`. For example, ` 15% ` means 15.
- The tip is calculated on the subtotal, before tax and service charges.
- When the value breaks more than one rule, only the first matching message is shown, in this order:
  1. empty
  2. not a number: anything other than digits with an optional single decimal point. This includes letters, commas, currency symbols, a minus sign, `e` notation and a second `%`.
  3. more than 2 decimal places
  4. above 100

### Number of people

- Spaces before and after the value are ignored.
- The value must be digits only, from 1 to 50. Leading zeros are allowed, so `03` means 3.
- Anything else is rejected, including `3.0`, `-3`, `3 people` and `1,000`.

### Names (Split by order)

- A name is optional, up to 30 characters, and may contain any characters.
- Spaces before and after a name are ignored.
- A name that is empty, or only spaces, is shown as "Person N", where N is the row's current position in the list.

### Tax and service charges

This is one optional field. Leaving it empty means 0. It covers GST, sales tax and any service charge printed on the receipt.

### Arithmetic

- All calculations use whole cents.
- The tip is rounded to the nearest cent, with exact halves rounded up. For example, 1.5 cents becomes 2 cents.
- Results must be exact at every allowed limit. At the maximum values, some intermediate products in the Split by order calculation exceed 9,007,199,254,740,991 (the largest whole number JavaScript's normal numbers store exactly). The implementation must therefore use exact integer arithmetic, for example BigInt. S-6 contains a test case for this.

### Display

- Results show 2 decimal places and comma thousands separators, for example `1,260.00`.
- No currency symbol is shown.
- Results use commas for readability, but money inputs reject commas. A result copied back into a field shows "Remove commas and currency symbols, e.g. 1250.50." This is a known limitation, recorded in the README.

### Limits

| Input | Allowed |
|---|---|
| Subtotal | 0.01 to 1,000,000.00 |
| Tax and service charges | 0 to 1,000,000.00 (empty = 0) |
| Ordered amount per person | 0.01 to 1,000,000.00 |
| Custom tip | 0 to 100, at most 2 decimal places |
| Number of people (Split evenly) | Whole number from 1 to 50 |
| People listed (Split by order) | 1 to 50 rows |
| Person's name | Optional, up to 30 characters |

### Error messages

| Case | Message |
|---|---|
| Subtotal empty | "Enter the bill subtotal." |
| Comma or currency symbol in any money input | "Remove commas and currency symbols, e.g. 1250.50." |
| Negative money input | "Amount can't be negative." |
| Money input is not a valid number | "Enter an amount using digits and an optional decimal point, e.g. 1250.50." |
| More than 2 decimal places (money input or custom tip) | "Use at most 2 decimal places." |
| Subtotal below 0.01 | "Subtotal must be at least 0.01." |
| Any money input above 1,000,000.00 | "Amount can't be more than 1,000,000.00." |
| Custom tip empty | "Enter a tip percentage." |
| Custom tip not a number, or above 100 | "Tip must be a number from 0 to 100." |
| Number of people invalid | "Number of people must be a whole number from 1 to 50." |
| Ordered amount empty or below 0.01 | "Enter what this person ordered (at least 0.01)." |

---

## Diner stories

### S-1: Enter the receipt amounts
**Serves:** J-1 · **Role:** Diner · **Status:** Not implemented · **Planned for:** v1

As a Diner, I want to enter the amounts printed on the receipt and be told straight away if something is wrong, so that the tip and split are based on the real bill.

**Normal case**
- Given the page has just opened, when I look at the form, then:
  - "Split evenly" is selected
  - "Subtotal" and "Tax and service charges" are empty
  - "10%" is selected
  - "Number of people" is 2
  - the results area says "Fill in the fields above to see the split."
- Given I enter subtotal `1000` and tax `160`, when the results appear, then they show "Subtotal 1,000.00", "Tax and service charges 160.00", "Tip (10%) 100.00" and "Total 1,260.00", in that order.
- Given I enter subtotal `1000` and leave tax empty, when the results appear, then they show "Tax and service charges 0.00".
- Given I enter subtotal ` 1000.50 ` with spaces around it, when the results appear, then they show "Subtotal 1,000.50".
- Given I enter subtotal `.5`, `12.` or `007`, when the results appear, then they show "Subtotal 0.50", "Subtotal 12.00" or "Subtotal 7.00" respectively.

**Invalid input**
- Given I click into the subtotal and leave it empty, when I move to the next field, then I see "Enter the bill subtotal." under the subtotal, and the results area says "Fix the highlighted fields to see the split."
- Given I enter subtotal `abc`, `12abc`, `+5` or `10.0.5`, when I leave the field, then I see "Enter an amount using digits and an optional decimal point, e.g. 1250.50." and no results are shown.
- Given I paste `1,250.50`, `Rs 1250`, `rs1250`, `1250Rs`, `$1250`, `1250 PKR` or `₨1,250` into the subtotal, when I leave the field, then I see "Remove commas and currency symbols, e.g. 1250.50." and no results are shown.
- Given I enter subtotal `-20`, when I leave the field, then I see "Amount can't be negative." and no results are shown.
- Given a valid subtotal, when I enter tax `abc` and leave the field, then I see "Enter an amount using digits and an optional decimal point, e.g. 1250.50." under the tax field and no results are shown.
- Given a valid subtotal, when I enter tax `-5` and leave the field, then I see "Amount can't be negative." under the tax field and no results are shown.
- Given a valid subtotal, when I enter tax `Rs 160` and leave the field, then I see "Remove commas and currency symbols, e.g. 1250.50." under the tax field and no results are shown.

**Boundary values**
- Given I enter subtotal `0` or `0.00`, when I leave the field, then I see "Subtotal must be at least 0.01." and no results are shown.
- Given I enter subtotal `0.01`, when the results appear, then they show "Subtotal 0.01".
- Given I enter subtotal `1`, when the results appear, then they show "Subtotal 1.00".
- Given I enter subtotal `1000000`, when the results appear, then they show "Subtotal 1,000,000.00".
- Given I enter subtotal `1000000.01`, when I leave the field, then I see "Amount can't be more than 1,000,000.00." and no results are shown.
- Given subtotal `1`, when I enter tax `0`, then no error is shown and the results show "Tax and service charges 0.00".
- Given subtotal `1`, when I enter tax `1000000` and leave the field, then no error is shown and the results show "Tax and service charges 1,000,000.00" and "Total 1,000,001.10".
- Given subtotal `1`, when I enter tax `1000000.01` and leave the field, then I see "Amount can't be more than 1,000,000.00." under the tax field and no results are shown.

**Very large and very small numbers**
- Given I enter subtotal `1e15`, when I leave the field, then I see "Enter an amount using digits and an optional decimal point, e.g. 1250.50."
- Given I enter subtotal `1000000000000000`, when I leave the field, then I see "Amount can't be more than 1,000,000.00."
- Given I enter subtotal `0.001` or `10.555`, when I leave the field, then I see "Use at most 2 decimal places."
- Given I enter tax `0.001`, when I leave the field, then I see "Use at most 2 decimal places." under the tax field.

**Carrying on after a result or an error**
- Given the subtotal shows an error, when I correct it to `1000`, then the error disappears as I type and results appear.
- Given results are shown for subtotal `100`, when I type `a` so the field reads `100a` and before I leave the field, then:
  - the results disappear straight away
  - the subtotal is outlined in red
  - the results area says "Fix the highlighted fields to see the split."

  When I then leave the field, I see "Enter an amount using digits and an optional decimal point, e.g. 1250.50."
- Given results are shown, when I change the subtotal to `abc` and then to `500`, then results reappear showing "Subtotal 500.00".
- Given both subtotal and tax show errors, when I fix only the subtotal, then no results are shown until the tax is fixed too.
- Given I have entered values and errors are showing on "Split evenly", when I press "Reset", then the form is as described in the first normal case, and no errors are shown.

### S-2: Choose a tip and see its amount
**Serves:** J-1 · **Role:** Diner · **Status:** Not implemented · **Planned for:** v1

As a Diner, I want to choose a common tip percentage or type my own and see the tip amount and grand total, so that I can settle on a fair tip quickly.

**Normal case**
- Given subtotal `1000` and tax `160`, when "10%" is selected, then I see "Tip (10%) 100.00" and "Total 1,260.00". The tip is calculated on the subtotal only.
- Given subtotal `1000` and tax `160`, when I select "20%", then the results update to "Tip (20%) 200.00" and "Total 1,360.00".
- Given subtotal `10.05` and tax empty, when I select "15%", then I see "Tip (15%) 1.51" (1.5075 rounded) and "Total 11.56".
- Given subtotal `200` and tax empty, when I select "Custom" and type `12.5` in "Custom tip (%)", then I see "Tip (12.5%) 25.00" and "Total 225.00".
- Given subtotal `200`, when I paste ` 15% ` into "Custom tip (%)", then it is read as 15 and I see "Tip (15%) 30.00".

**Invalid input**
- Given I select "Custom" and leave "Custom tip (%)" empty, when I leave the field, then I see "Enter a tip percentage." and no results are shown.
- Given I enter custom tip `ten`, `-5`, `-0.001`, `1,5`, `$15` or `15%%`, when I leave the field, then I see "Tip must be a number from 0 to 100." and no results are shown.

**Boundary values**
- Given subtotal `1000` and tax `160`, when I select "0%", then I see "Tip (0%) 0.00" and "Total 1,160.00". When I enter custom tip `0`, then I see the same amounts.
- Given subtotal `1000`, when I enter custom tip `100`, then I see "Tip (100%) 1,000.00".
- Given I enter custom tip `100.01`, when I leave the field, then I see "Tip must be a number from 0 to 100."
- Given I enter custom tip `100.001`, when I leave the field, then I see "Use at most 2 decimal places." This rule is checked before the range.
- Given subtotal `0.10` and "15%", when the results appear, then I see "Tip (15%) 0.02" (exactly 1.5 cents, rounded up) and "Total 0.12".
- Given subtotal `0.05` and "10%", when the results appear, then I see "Tip (10%) 0.01" (exactly 0.5 cents, rounded up) and "Total 0.06".

**Very large and very small numbers**
- Given subtotal `1000000`, tax `1000000` and custom tip `100`, when the results appear, then I see "Tip (100%) 1,000,000.00" and "Total 3,000,000.00" exactly.
- Given subtotal `1000000`, when I enter custom tip `0.01`, then I see "Tip (0.01%) 100.00".
- Given subtotal `0.01` and "10%", when the results appear, then I see "Tip (10%) 0.00" (0.1 cent rounds down) and "Total 0.01".
- Given I enter custom tip `1e15`, when I leave the field, then I see "Tip must be a number from 0 to 100."
- Given I enter custom tip `0.001`, when I leave the field, then I see "Use at most 2 decimal places."

**Carrying on after a result or an error**
- Given results are shown for "10%" and subtotal `1000`, when I change the subtotal to `2000`, then the results show "Tip (10%) 200.00" without pressing any button.
- Given custom tip shows "Tip must be a number from 0 to 100.", when I select "15%", then the error disappears and results appear using 15%.
- Given I then select "Custom" again, when I look at "Custom tip (%)", then it still holds what I typed, its error is shown again and no results are shown.

### S-3: Split the total evenly so the shares add up exactly
**Serves:** J-2 · **Role:** Diner · **Status:** Not implemented · **Planned for:** v1

As a Diner, I want the grand total split evenly between the number of people, with any leftover cents shown openly, so that the shares add up exactly to the bill.

Display rule:
- When every share is equal, one line shows "Each person pays X".
- Otherwise there are two lines, with the higher share first, each using "1 person pays" or "N people pay".
- A final line shows "N shares add up to TOTAL", or "1 share adds up to TOTAL" when there is 1 person.

**Normal case**
- Given a total of 1,260.00, when I enter 4 people, then I see "Each person pays 315.00" and "4 shares add up to 1,260.00".
- Given a total of 100.00 (subtotal `100`, tax empty, "0%"), when I enter 3 people, then I see "1 person pays 33.34", "2 people pay 33.33" and "3 shares add up to 100.00".
- Given a total of 1,260.00, when I enter ` 4 ` or `04`, then I see "Each person pays 315.00".

**Invalid input**
- Given I clear the number of people, or enter `two`, `3 people`, `-3`, `2.5`, `3.0` or `1,000`, when I leave the field, then I see "Number of people must be a whole number from 1 to 50." and no results are shown.

**Boundary values**
- Given I enter `0` people, when I leave the field, then I see "Number of people must be a whole number from 1 to 50."
- Given a total of 1,260.00, when I enter 1 person, then I see "Each person pays 1,260.00" and "1 share adds up to 1,260.00".
- Given a total of 1,260.00, when I enter 50 people, then I see "Each person pays 25.20" and "50 shares add up to 1,260.00".
- Given I enter `51` people, when I leave the field, then I see "Number of people must be a whole number from 1 to 50."

**Very large and very small numbers**
- Given a total of 3,000,000.00, when I enter 7 people, then I see "6 people pay 428,571.43", "1 person pays 428,571.42" and "7 shares add up to 3,000,000.00".
- Given a total of 3,000,000.00, when I enter 50 people, then I see "Each person pays 60,000.00".
- Given a total of 0.02 (subtotal `0.02`, "0%"), when I enter 3 people, then I see "2 people pay 0.01", "1 person pays 0.00" and "3 shares add up to 0.02".
- Given a total of 0.01 (subtotal `0.01`, "0%"), when I enter 50 people, then I see "1 person pays 0.01", "49 people pay 0.00" and "50 shares add up to 0.01".
- Given I enter `1e15` or `0.001` people, when I leave the field, then I see "Number of people must be a whole number from 1 to 50."

**Carrying on after a result or an error**
- Given a total of 1,260.00 and results shown for 3 people, when I change it to 4, then I see "Each person pays 315.00" without pressing any button.
- Given results are shown, when I change the number of people to `two`, then the results disappear straight away and the field is outlined in red. When I correct it to `2`, then I see "Each person pays 630.00" for a total of 1,260.00.
- Given I have entered values on "Split evenly", when I press "Reset", then the form is as described in the first normal case of S-1.

### S-4: Round everyone's share up to a whole amount
**Serves:** J-2 · **Role:** Diner · **Status:** Not implemented · **Planned for:** Backlog

As a Diner, I want the option for everyone to pay the same share rounded up to a whole number, with the extra added to the tip, so that we can pay in notes or round transfers.

**Normal case**
- Given a total of 100.00 and 3 people, when I turn on "Round up shares", then I see "Each person pays 34.00", "Extra tip from rounding: 2.00" and "3 shares add up to 102.00".
- Given a total of 1,260.00 and 4 people, when I turn on "Round up shares", then I see "Each person pays 315.00" and "Extra tip from rounding: 0.00".

**Invalid input**
- Given "Round up shares" is on, when I enter `two` people and leave the field, then I see "Number of people must be a whole number from 1 to 50." and no results are shown. When I correct it to `3` for a total of 100.00, then I see "Each person pays 34.00" again.

**Boundary values**
- Given a total of 0.01 and 1 person, when I turn on "Round up shares", then I see "Each person pays 1.00" and "Extra tip from rounding: 0.99".
- Given a total of 1,260.00 and 50 people, when I turn on "Round up shares", then I see "Each person pays 26.00" and "Extra tip from rounding: 40.00".

**Very large and very small numbers**
- Given a total of 3,000,000.00 and 7 people, when I turn on "Round up shares", then I see "Each person pays 428,572.00" and "Extra tip from rounding: 4.00".
- Given a total of 0.02 and 3 people, when I turn on "Round up shares", then I see "Each person pays 1.00" and "Extra tip from rounding: 2.98".

**Carrying on after a result or an error**
- Given "Round up shares" is on with a total of 100.00, when I change 3 people to 4, then I see "Each person pays 25.00" and "Extra tip from rounding: 0.00".
- Given "Round up shares" is on, when I turn it off, then the exact shares from S-3 are shown again.
- Given "Round up shares" is on, when I press "Reset", then it is turned off.

## Bill Organiser stories

### S-10: Enter the receipt amounts when splitting by order
**Serves:** J-3 · **Role:** Bill Organiser · **Status:** Not implemented · **Planned for:** v1

As a Bill Organiser, I want to enter the receipt amounts and tip while splitting by order, so that each person's share of tax and tip is based on the real bill.

The receipt fields follow the same rules and messages as in S-1 and S-2. The criteria below check them in "Split by order".

**Normal case**
- Given the page has just opened, when I select "Split by order", then:
  - "Subtotal" and "Tax and service charges" are empty
  - "10%" is selected
  - there are 2 empty unnamed rows
  - the results area says "Fill in the fields above to see the split."
- Given "Split by order" with subtotal `100`, tax `16` and "10%", and Ali ordered `60` and Sara ordered `40`, when the results appear, then they show "Subtotal 100.00", "Tax and service charges 16.00", "Tip (10%) 10.00" and "Total 126.00", followed by the table from S-6.
- Given the same values, when I select "Custom" and type `12.5`, then I see:
  - "Tip (12.5%) 12.50" and "Total 128.50"
  - Ali: Share of tax and tip 17.10, Owes 77.10
  - Sara: Share of tax and tip 11.40, Owes 51.40
  - a total row of 128.50 with "Matches the receipt total."

**Invalid input**
- Given "Split by order" with valid rows, when I enter subtotal `abc` and leave the field, then I see "Enter an amount using digits and an optional decimal point, e.g. 1250.50." and no amounts owed are shown.
- Given "Split by order" with valid rows, when I enter subtotal `Rs 100` and leave the field, then I see "Remove commas and currency symbols, e.g. 1250.50." and no amounts owed are shown.
- Given "Split by order" with valid rows, when I enter tax `-5` and leave the field, then I see "Amount can't be negative." under the tax field and no amounts owed are shown.
- Given "Split by order" with valid rows, when I enter custom tip `ten` and leave the field, then I see "Tip must be a number from 0 to 100." and no amounts owed are shown.

**Boundary values**
- Given subtotal `100`, tax `16`, and Ali `60` and Sara `40`, when I select "0%", then:
  - Ali: Share of tax and tip 9.60, Owes 69.60
  - Sara: Share of tax and tip 6.40, Owes 46.40
  - the total row shows 116.00
- Given "Split by order", when I enter subtotal `0` and leave the field, then I see "Subtotal must be at least 0.01."
- Given "Split by order", when I enter subtotal `1000000.01` and leave the field, then I see "Amount can't be more than 1,000,000.00."

**Very large and very small numbers**
- Given "Split by order", when I enter subtotal `1e15` and leave the field, then I see "Enter an amount using digits and an optional decimal point, e.g. 1250.50."
- Given "Split by order", when I enter subtotal `0.001` and leave the field, then I see "Use at most 2 decimal places."
- The largest and smallest valid receipts are checked in S-6.

**Carrying on after a result or an error**
- Given subtotal `100`, tax `16` and "10%", and Ali `60` and Sara `40`, when I select "20%", then:
  - Ali owes 81.60 and Sara owes 54.40
  - the total row shows 136.00 with "Matches the receipt total."
- Given I entered subtotal `100` on "Split by order", when I switch to "Split evenly", then "Subtotal" shows `100`.
- Given values and errors on "Split by order", when I press "Reset", then the receipt fields and rows are as described in the first normal case, no errors are shown, and "Split by order" stays selected.

### S-5: List each person and what they ordered
**Serves:** J-3 · **Role:** Bill Organiser · **Status:** Not implemented · **Planned for:** v1

As a Bill Organiser, I want to list each person with the amount they ordered, so that each person's amount owed is based on their own order.

**Normal case**
- Given "Split evenly" with 4 people and a subtotal, tax and tip entered, when I select "Split by order" for the first time, then the subtotal, tax and tip are kept and I see 2 rows labelled "Person 1" and "Person 2", each with an empty "Ordered" field.
- Given I then switch back to "Split evenly", when I look at "Number of people", then it still shows 4.
- Given 2 rows, when I press "Add person", then a row "Person 3" appears with an empty "Ordered" field.
- Given 3 unnamed rows with amounts `10`, `20` and `30`, when I press "Remove" on the second row, then it is removed, and the remaining rows are "Person 1" with `10` and "Person 2" with `30`.
- Given I type the name `Ali` in row 1, when results appear, then row 1 is labelled "Ali". When I clear the name, then it is labelled "Person 1" again.
- Given I type a name of only spaces in row 1, when results appear, then row 1 is labelled "Person 1".
- Given I am on "Split by order", when I switch to "Split evenly" and back, then my rows, names and amounts are still there.

### S-6: See what each person owes, with tax and tip shared in proportion
**Serves:** J-3 · **Role:** Bill Organiser · **Status:** Not implemented · **Planned for:** v1

As a Bill Organiser, I want to see what each person owes, made up of their order plus a share of tax, charges and tip in proportion to their order, so that nobody pays for someone else's food.

How shares are worked out:
- Each person's share of tax and tip is their ordered amount divided by the total of all ordered amounts, multiplied by tax plus tip.
- Each share is rounded down to the cent.
- Leftover cents go one at a time to the people with the largest remainders. Ties go to the person higher in the list.

input.content:
# Scope and Decisions

**Scope status: Locked on 17 October 2026, before the build started.**

**Change control.** After the lock, a change to scope or behaviour must follow these steps in order:
1. Update `user-stories.md` first.
2. Add a row to the change log at the end of this file.
3. Only then ask the AI coding tool to change the code.

The code is never allowed to drift from the documents.

## In scope for v1

| Story | Serves | Role |
|---|---|---|
| S-1 Enter the receipt amounts | J-1 | Diner |
| S-2 Choose a tip and see its amount | J-1 | Diner |
| S-3 Split the total evenly so the shares add up exactly | J-2 | Diner |
| S-10 Enter the receipt amounts when splitting by order | J-3 | Bill Organiser |
| S-5 List each person and what they ordered | J-3 | Bill Organiser |
| S-6 See what each person owes, with tax and tip shared in proportion | J-3 | Bill Organiser |
| S-7 Be warned when the amounts don't cover the bill | J-4 | Bill Organiser |

## Backlog (written, not built)

| Story | Serves | Role |
|---|---|---|
| S-4 Round everyone's share up to a whole amount | J-2 | Diner |
| S-8 Split a shared item between several people | J-3 | Bill Organiser |
| S-9 Copy a summary of who owes what | J-5 | Bill Organiser |

## Out of scope

These have no story and will not be built:
- Choosing or converting currencies. No currency symbol is shown.
- Locale formats, such as a decimal comma (`12,50`) or Indian digit grouping (`1,00,000`).
- Entering individual menu items. Each person's order is entered as one amount.
- Saving bills, history, accounts or links to share.
- Scanning receipts, or taking payments or payment requests.
- Separate tip rules for service charges. Tax and service charges is one field, and it is never tipped on.
- Translation into other languages.

## Decisions log

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| D-1 | Scope for 2 to 4 hours | Diner flow and Organiser flow both in v1. Shared items, round-up and copy summary in the backlog. |
| D-2 | What is entered | Subtotal, plus one optional "Tax and service charges" amount. Tip is a percentage. |
| D-3 | What the tip is calculated on | The subtotal before tax and service charges. Rounded to the cent, with exact halves rounded up. |
| D-4 | Leftover cents in an even split | Uneven shares are shown openly. For example, "1 person pays 33.34, 2 people pay 33.33", always adding up exactly to the total. |
| D-5 | Leftover cents in a split by order | Largest remainder first. Ties go to the person higher in the list. |
| D-6 | Currency and precision | One currency, no symbol, 2 decimal places. All maths in whole cents, using exact integer arithmetic (BigInt) because maximum-value products exceed JavaScript's safe integer limit. |
| D-7 | Limits | Subtotal 0.01 to 1,000,000.00. Tax 0 to 1,000,000.00. Tip 0 to 100%. 1 to 50 people. Names up to 30 characters. |
| D-8 | Invalid input | Rejected with a specific message. Never silently rounded or corrected. The only exceptions are surrounding spaces and a single trailing `%` on the tip, which are ignored. |
| D-9 | Commas and currency symbols | Rejected with their own message rather than stripped, to avoid guessing whether a comma is a thousands separator or a decimal point. |
| D-10 | Ordered amounts that don't match the receipt | Allowed, with a warning that states the exact gap. Amounts owed are still shown. |
| D-11 | Validation timing | Checked and recalculated on every keystroke. Results disappear straight away when an input is invalid. Message text appears when the user leaves the field. |
| D-12 | Reset | Clears everything, including both modes, and keeps the currently selected mode. |
| D-13 | Switching mode | Receipt fields are shared between modes. The people count and the people list are kept separately. |
| D-14 | "Must never" statements | About correctness, not permissions, because the app has no accounts. |
| D-15 | Stack | Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript (ES modules), with no build step and no dependencies. The calculation logic sits in a pure module, separate from the page. |
| D-16 | Tests | Unit tests for the calculation module using Node's built-in test runner (`node --test`, Node 20 or later). The acceptance criteria are still checked by hand in the browser. |
| D-17 | Running locally | Served over HTTP with `npx serve` or `python3 -m http.server`, because browsers block ES modules opened directly from a `file://` path. The README must say this. |
| D-18 | Live URL | GitHub Pages, in addition to the local instructions, not instead of them. |

## Accepted gaps

These were raised in review and accepted as they are. Each one will be stated in the README.
- **J-1, deciding what tip is fair.** The presets (0%, 10%, 15%, 20%) are the app's guidance on common tip levels. There is no advice on local customs, to avoid making claims about specific countries.
- **J-5, telling each person their amount.** This is served only by a backlog story (S-9), so v1 does not help with it.
- **Commas in output but not input.** Results show `1,260.00` with commas, but inputs reject commas, so a result copied back into a field gets an error message (see D-9).

## Definition of done for a story

A story is marked **Implemented** only when all three of these are true:
1. Every one of its acceptance criteria has been checked by hand in the running app, in a current browser.
2. Any calculation it relies on is covered by a passing unit test.
3. Its status has been updated in `user-stories.md` and the change is noted in the README.

If any criterion fails and isn't fixed, the story stays **Not implemented**, and the README says which criterion failed.

## Change log

| Date | Change | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| 17 Oct 2026 | Scope locked | Review complete |

# Technical plan

## Stack: plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with no build step

Your constraint left the stack open. I recommend plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, which is what we already locked in D-15.

| | Plain HTML/JS (recommended) | Vite + TypeScript + Vitest |
|---|---|---|
| Reviewer setup | Node 20, then `npm start` | Node, `npm install` (downloads about 30 MB), then `npm run dev` |
| Dependencies | None | Vite, TypeScript, Vitest and what they depend on |
| Build step | None. The files that run are the files you wrote | Yes, and a failed build blocks the reviewer |
| What it adds | Nothing to break | Type checking, which mostly catches mistakes that tests also catch here |

The app is about 10 input fields and some arithmetic. Each dependency is one more thing that can fail on a reviewer's clean machine. With no dependencies there's no `node_modules`, so nothing needs leaving out of the package.

- **Prerequisite: Node.js 20 or later.** It runs both the tests (Node's built-in test runner) and a tiny local server.
- **The local server is needed** because browsers refuse to load JavaScript modules from a page opened straight from disk (`file://`). Without a server, the reviewer would see a blank page.
- **The server is written with Node's own `http` module**, so it uses no packages and works offline.

## Folder structure

```
firstname-lastname-calculator/
  README.md
  package.json          # scripts only ("start", "test"), no dependencies
  scripts/
    serve.js            # ~30-line static server for src/ on http://localhost:8080
  src/
    index.html          # markup: labels, fields, results area
    styles.css
    app.js              # UI only: holds state, listens to events, renders
    lib/                # pure logic, no DOM, so it's fully unit-testable
      money.js          # text → BigInt cents, BigInt cents → "1,260.00"
      validate.js       # parse each input type, apply message precedence
      calc.js           # tip, even split, proportional allocation, receipt check
      messages.js       # every exact message string and template, in one place
      engine.js         # compute(state) → everything the screen should show
  tests/
    money.test.js
    validate.test.js
    calc.test.js
    engine.test.js      # acceptance criteria written as tests
    manual-checklist.md # UI criteria to check by hand, per browser
  docs/                 # the four locked documents
  transcripts/
  .github/workflows/pages.yml   # optional, for the live URL
```

**The key design choice is `engine.js`.** It takes the raw state: every field's text, which fields the user has left, and the selected mode. It returns everything the screen should show:
- the error message for each field, and which fields are outlined in red
- the results-area message
- the exact result lines, such as "1 person pays 33.34"

`app.js` then only copies those strings into the page. Most of the acceptance criteria, including exact message text, the "Fix the highlighted fields" logic and the display wording, can therefore be tested automatically without a browser. Only the parts that need a real page, such as clicking, leaving a field and disabled buttons, are left for the manual checklist.

## How money avoids floating-point errors

The rule: **money is never a JavaScript Number. It's a BigInt count of cents from the moment it's read to the moment it's displayed.**

1. **Reading input.** Text like `"1000.5"` is checked against a strict pattern and split at the decimal point. The two parts are joined into an integer as text: `"1000"` + `"50"` becomes `100050n` cents. `parseFloat`, `Number()` and `toFixed()` are never used on money. 2. **Tip percentage.** It's stored as a BigInt in hundredths of a percent, so 12.5% becomes `1250n`.
3. **Tip calculation.** `tip = (subtotal × percent + 5000n) / 10000n`. BigInt division truncates, so adding 5000n first gives the "exact halves round up" rule. That works because every value is zero or positive.
4. **Even split.** `share = total / n` and `leftover = total % n`, all in whole cents.
5. **Split by order.** The share calculation multiplies an extra amount by an ordered amount, and at the maximum values that product is about 2×10¹⁶. That's above 2⁵³, the largest integer a Number holds exactly, and that's why it's BigInt and not just whole-number Numbers.
6. **Display.** The digits are split into whole and decimal parts by hand, and commas are inserted every three digits. `toLocaleString` isn't used, so the output doesn't change with the reviewer's computer language settings.

## How each acceptance criterion will be tested

- **Automated tests**, run with `npm test`. Each test is named after its story and category, for example `S-3 large: 3,000,000.00 split 7 ways`, so a reviewer can map each test to its criterion.
- **A manual checklist**, `tests/manual-checklist.md`. It lists every criterion that needs a real browser, with a tick box per browser and the date it was checked.

| Story | Automated tests (`engine.test.js` and the unit tests) | Checked by hand |
|---|---|---|
| S-1 Receipt amounts | Every parse result, every message and the precedence order. Empty-and-left versus never-left. The "Fix…" and "Fill in…" logic. Results lines | Error appears on leaving the field. The red outline appears while typing, before leaving. Reset |

| S-3 Even split | Every split, the singular and plural wording, and people-field parsing | Results update while typing. Reset |
| S-10 Organiser receipt | Every value, using both modes' state | Fields shared across modes. Reset keeps the mode |
| S-5 People list | Amount validation, "Person N" labels, renumbering after a removal, names of only spaces | Add and remove. Remove disabled at 1 row, Add disabled at 50. 30-character name cap, including paste. Mode switching keeps the list |
| S-6 Amounts owed | Every value, including the tie, the largest-remainder case and the BigInt maximum case | Live updates in the browser |
| S-7 Mismatch warning | Every warning and total-row message, including the boundary 0.01 and the maximum cases | Warning appears and disappears live |

- **The app must be served over HTTP.** Opening `index.html` directly shows a blank page. `npm start` handles this, and `python3 -m http.server` run in `src/` is the fallback if Node isn't installed.

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|

| Results lag behind an invalid value while the user is still typing | One rule: every keystroke runs `compute(state)`, which returns no results whenever any input is invalid. Tested in `engine.test.js` |
| Manual testing runs over the 2–4 hour budget | Most criteria are automated through `engine.js`. The manual list covers only interaction |
| Safari can't be tested without Apple hardware | State honestly in the README which browsers were tested by hand. Don't claim Safari unless it was checked |
